Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC DoS based on ASN.1 decoder read overrun
Vulnerabilities.Description: In all released versions of MIT krb5, an unauthenticated attacker can cause a KDC process to perform a large read overrun, likely causing the process to terminate.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS in RPCSEC_GSS buffer decode failure
Vulnerabilities.Description: The RPCSEC_GSS authentication routines in lib/rpc/authgss_prot.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.4 and later do not free partially decoded buffers on failure, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak in kadmind) via crafted RPCSEC_GSS messages.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory leak DoS in xdr_krb5_tl_data() decode failure
Vulnerabilities.Description: xdr_krb5_tl_data() in lib/kadm5/kadm_rpc_xdr.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free partially decoded data on failure, which allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (memory leak in kadmind) via crafted RPC requests that trigger a decode failure.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated memory leak DoS in KDB keytab key decryption error path
Vulnerabilities.Description: krb5_ktkdb_get_entry() in lib/kdb/keytab.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.2.8 and later does not free decrypted key material when a post-decryption check fails, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak in the KDC or kadmind) via requests that repeatedly trigger key decryption failures.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated DoS exploiting dereference of null policy name pointers
Vulnerabilities.Description: The policy RPC stubs in kadmin/server/server_stubs.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.3 and later do not reject a NULL policy name decoded by xdr_nullstring(), which allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (kadmind crash via NULL pointer dereference) by sending a policy request with an empty policy name that reaches authorization checks or logging code.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory exhaustion DoS via unbounded RPC XDR allocation
Vulnerabilities.Description: The GSS-RPC layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not enforce size limits on XDR-decoded data, which allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion or excessive CPU consumption in kadmind) via crafted RPC requests that trigger unbounded memory allocations during XDR decoding.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via GSS-RPC auth flavor switching
Vulnerabilities.Description: The GSS-RPC transport layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.4 and later does not release the previous authentication context when a client switches from an RPCSEC_GSS or AUTH_GSSAPI flavor to a non-GSS flavor on the same TCP connection. This allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) by repeatedly establishing and abandoning GSS authentication contexts.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT error paths
Vulnerabilities.Description: The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free decoded arguments on certain error paths, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) via crafted AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests that trigger authentication failures.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated CPU DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI client states cleanup
Vulnerabilities.Description: clean_client() in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) restarts its scan from the head of the client list after each removal, resulting in quadratic CPU cost. Remote attackers can cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in kadmind) by accumulating a large number of AUTH_GSSAPI client entries.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion via failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests
Vulnerabilities.Description: The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.2 and later allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) by sending repeated failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests. Each failed request allocates client state that is only freed after a 15-minute expiration timeout, allowing an attacker to accumulate memory faster than it is reclaimed.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: kadmind: request alteration and protected information disclosure
Vulnerabilities.Description: In MIT krb5 release 1.4 and later, an active network attacker can alter the arguments sent by a legitimate client to RPC services protected by RPCSEC_GSS, or cause return values to be sent in plain text.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding
Vulnerabilities.Description: decode_sequence_of() in lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 and later grows the decoded element array one entry at a time, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in the KDC) by sending an unauthenticated AS-REQ or TGS-REQ with a large number of elements in a SEQUENCE OF field over TCP.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT Kerberos 5: Denial of Service via NULL pointer dereference in NegoEx mechanism
Vulnerabilities.Description: In MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) before 1.22.3, there is a NULL pointer dereference if an application calls gss_accept_sec_context() on a system with a NegoEx mechanism registered in /etc/gss/mech. An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger this, causing the process to terminate in parse_nego_message.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT Kerberos 5 (krb5): Denial of Service via integer underflow and out-of-bounds read
Vulnerabilities.Description: In MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) before 1.22.3, there is an integer underflow and resultant out-of-bounds read if an application calls gss_accept_sec_context() on a system with a NegoEx mechanism registered in /etc/gss/mech. An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger this, possibly causing the process to terminate in parse_message.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: Alteration of authentication indicators in CAMMAC container
Vulnerabilities.Description: In MIT krb5 release 1.14 and later (since authentication indicator support was added), an authenticated attacker can bypass authentication indicator requirements using an unkeyed checksum in the CAMMAC authdata container.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request
Vulnerabilities.Description: If a KDC is configured to allow PKINIT authentication, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference, causing the process to terminate.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via malformed PAC in S4U2Proxy requests
Vulnerabilities.Description: MIT krb5 through 1.22.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the KDC's get_pac_princ_with_realm() that returns success while leaving the client principal NULL on malformed names. A malicious or compromised cross-realm trusted KDC can send an S4U2Proxy request with a PAC carrying a malformed client name to crash krb5kdc and deny authentication.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via crafted forwarded credentials
Vulnerabilities.Description: MIT Kerberos 5 (krb5) through 1.22.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference in make_cred_list() in rd_cred.c that allows authenticated Kerberos clients to crash services by sending mismatched KRB-CRED arrays. Attackers can send forwarded credentials with more tickets than ticket_info entries through gss_accept_sec_context() to crash GSS-API acceptor services, causing denial of service.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: Unauthorized key reset of protected principal via kpasswd
Vulnerabilities.Description: In MIT krb5 release 1.15 and later, a client with kadmin administrative privileges can bypass the lockdown_keys attribute by using the password change protocol instead of the kadmin protocol.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: Improper authorization via flawed PAC checksum verification
Vulnerabilities.Description: In MIT krb5 release 1.21 and later, server applications will erroneously treat the PAC within a ticket as verified when the server checksum is invalid.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 GSS-RPC client memory leak on XID mismatch retries
Vulnerabilities.Description: clnttcp_call() in lib/rpc/clnt_tcp.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free the RPC reply verifier between retries, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak in GSS-RPC client programs) by injecting RPC replies with mismatched XIDs or by triggering authentication retries.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via crafted EC certificate in CMS encryption
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Encrypting a CMS message to an EC certificate whose group order
is 1 may cause CMS_encrypt() or CMS_encrypt_ex() to loop indefinitely.

Impact summary: An attacker able to supply the recipient certificate to an
application performing CMS encryption can cause that application to loop
indefinitely, consuming CPU and resulting in Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

Description: CMS_encrypt() and CMS_encrypt_ex() encrypt a message to one or
more recipient certificates and, for an EC recipient, generate an ephemeral
key in the recipient's group. If the certificate declares a group order of 1,
random scalar generation can only produce zero. The key generation routine
then retries without limit while waiting for a nonzero private scalar, so the
call never returns.

The OpenSSL TLS and QUIC implementations do not use this path. An application
is exposed only if it calls CMS_encrypt() or CMS_encrypt_ex() with a recipient
certificate whose EC parameters are attacker-controlled. Certificates with
normal EC group orders do not trigger the loop.

OpenSSL 4.0 and later reject unknown explicit EC groups in default builds.
These versions are affected only when configured with the
enable-ec_explicit_curves option.

The result is a hang that consumes a CPU core until the process is
interrupted, a Denial of Service. The severity is Low because the attacker
must supply the recipient certificate and the application must choose to
encrypt to it; ordinary CMS encryption to trusted recipients is unaffected.

The fix makes EC key generation fail when the group has no valid nonzero
private scalar, instead of retrying indefinitely.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules in 4.1, 4.0, 3.5 and 3.0 are not affected. The FIPS provider
does not support arbitrary explicit EC domain parameters, so an order-1 group
is rejected during key import before the vulnerable key generation path is
reached.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via overlapping QUIC CRYPTO frame processing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A retransmitted QUIC CRYPTO frame can release packet storage
while the TLS record layer retains a direct pointer into that storage causing
use after free.

Impact summary: A malicious QUIC server can cause a heap-use-after-free read
in the OpenSSL QUIC client. The server can also identify one allocator-adjacent
byte through the client's protected Handshake response.

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Description: During CRYPTO stream processing, a pointer into the first frame's
memory on the stream is lent to the TLS handshake processing. The memory
must remain stable until it is processed and released. However the processing
of retransmitted CRYPTO frames could release the memory if the retransmitted
frame fully overlapped the existing frame. This then causes use-after-free read
when the TLS handshake processing continues.

The use-after-free read can lead to a Denial-of-Service of the client
application or a minor leak of information about the heap memory contents
that might be overwritten with other data, subsequently allocated by
the application, to the peer.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation is outside of
the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: OpenSSL: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in AES-GCM-SIV
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Setting an AES-GCM-SIV IV shorter than the expected nonce
length via EVP_CipherInit_ex() may trigger a heap out-of-bounds read.
Supplying a longer IV is silently truncated instead of rejected.

Impact summary: An application passing a caller-supplied IV of the wrong
length may crash or read beyond its buffer. Because trailing IV bytes are
ignored, an attacker who knows one message and tag may forge messages under a
different IV.

CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read

Description: AES-GCM-SIV copies the caller-supplied IV or nonce into its
internal state using a copy whose length is taken from the expected nonce size
rather than from the length the caller actually provided. When the caller
passes a shorter IV, the copy reads past the end of the caller's buffer;
AddressSanitizer confirms a heap out-of-bounds read reached through
EVP_CipherInit_ex() into ossl_aes_gcm_siv_init(). When the caller passes a
longer IV, the implementation silently discards the trailing bytes instead of
rejecting the length.

The truncation breaks the binding between the IV and the computed
authentication tag. An attacker who has observed a message and its tag under
one IV can produce a message and tag that verify under a different IV whose
first bytes match, since the surplus bytes never influence the computation.
The message itself is unchanged, so this is a failure of IV commitment rather
than a classic existential forgery.

Only applications that call EVP_CipherInit_ex() (or the equivalent provider
cipher initialization) with an IV length other than the standard 12 bytes for
AES-GCM-SIV are affected. The severity is limited because the out-of-bounds
read is small and attacker-controlled only in length, and the forgery requires
an unusual IV length choice by the application.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules are not affected by this issue, as AES-GCM-SIV is not an
approved algorithm.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Information disclosure via uninitialized memory in QUIC peer detection
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: QUIC, when performing automated peer detection, may allow
uninitialized stack data to leak into the received address which is then used
as the destination for outgoing packets.

Impact summary: Applications using QUIC's automated peer detection mechanism
may receive an invalid address, leading to connection loss and disclosure of
uninitialized stack data to an attacker observing the outgoing network traffic.

CWE: CWE-457 (Use of Uninitialized Variable)

Description: The OpenSSL QUIC stack contains a feature in which, when using an
already connected socket, it will auto-detect the peer address during the SSL
handshake.  This feature uses the getpeername() function, passing a buffer of
sufficient length to hold any supported address family, but passes a buffer
length that is only sized such that larger addresses, such as IPv6, cannot be
retrieved. The getpeername() function however, still returns the full address
length, which is accepted as the valid input buffer length, leading to the
address buffer containing uninitialized stack data instead of the actual peer
address. The invalid peer address is then used as destination for the outgoing
packets which leads to a connectivity breakage and a leakage of the
uninitialized stack data to passive network observers.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules in 4.0, 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.0 are not affected by this CVE as
the affected protocol is not implemented in the FIPS module.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: OpenSSL: Message authentication bypass via zero-length AAD update
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: The AES-GCM-SIV implementation treats a zero-length Additional
Authenticated Data (AAD) update as a reset of all the AAD supplied so far,
instead of leaving the AAD unchanged. An application that supplies its AAD in
several fragments, one of which is empty, therefore produces or verifies
messages whose authentication tag does not cover the AAD supplied before
the empty fragment.

Impact summary: Data an application intended to authenticate alongside a
message is silently left unauthenticated. An attacker can forge the AAD of such
a message.

CWE: CWE-325: Missing Cryptographic Step

Description: An application passing AAD in multiple chunks of which some have
zero length will have the previous AAD chunks effectively unauthenticated. Also,
on context re-initialisation, the AAD was not reset, which meant that any AAD
accumulated from the previous context usage were also included in the AAD of the
new message.

The fix makes a zero-length AAD update a no-op and clears any accumulated AAD
whenever the context is re-initialised with a key or a nonce.
A re-initialisation that only changes parameters keeps the AAD.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules are not affected, as AES-GCM-SIV is not a FIPS approved
algorithm and is implemented only in the default provider, outside the
OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

accumulated from the previous context usage were also included in the AAD of the
new message.

The fix makes a zero-length AAD update a no-op and clears any accumulated AAD
whenever the context is re-initialised with a key or a nonce.
A re-initialisation that only changes parameters keeps the AAD.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules are not affected, as AES-GCM-SIV is not a FIPS approved
algorithm and is implemented only in the default provider, outside the
OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libxml2: libxml2: Information disclosure, SSRF, or denial of service due to improper parseFlags propagation.
Vulnerabilities.Description: In xinclude in libxml2 before 2.15.4, xmlXIncludeProcess and xmlXIncludeProcessTree do not propagate parseFlags. This has security relevance for, for example, the XML_PARSE_NONET flag, if (without it) a custom resource loader accesses the internet and triggers XML external entity injection, SSRF, or a denial of service (e.g., for an attacker-controlled internet resource that is intentionally slow).

Vulnerabilities.Title: chromium-browser: Use after free in XML
Vulnerabilities.Description: Use after free in XML in Google Chrome prior to 157.0.8103.50 allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

Vulnerabilities.Title: chromium-browser: chromium-browser: Type confusion in XML
Vulnerabilities.Description: Type confusion in XML in Google Chrome prior to 153.0.8010.36 allowed a remote attacker to potentially execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: Medium)

Vulnerabilities.Title: chromium-browser: Use after free in XML
Vulnerabilities.Description: Use after free in XML in Google Chrome prior to 148.0.7778.216 allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

Vulnerabilities.Title: libxslt: use-after-free with key data stored cross-RVT
Vulnerabilities.Description: A use-after-free vulnerability was found in libxslt while parsing xsl nodes that may lead to the dereference of expired pointers and application crash.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffe ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer vulnerability in OSGeo gdal (frmts/zlib/contrib/infback9 modules). This vulnerability is associated with program files inftree9.C‎.

This issue affects gdal: before 3.11.0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: github.com/moby/sys/user: moby/sys/user: Denial of Service via crafted user or group database files
Vulnerabilities.Description: The `github.com/moby/sys/user` package provides Go utilities for parsing and looking up entries in Unix-style user and group database files. Versions before 0.4.1 do not sufficiently limit entries when parsing `/etc/passwd`- or `/etc/group`-style files, allowing an attacker who can supply a specially crafted file to cause excessive memory consumption and potentially terminate the affected process due to an out-of-memory condition. This issue is patched in version 0.4.1. As a workaround, avoid parsing attacker-controlled user or group database files, or validate and limit untrusted input before parsing it.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Invoking integer overflow in NewNTUnicodeString in golang.org/x/sys/windows
Vulnerabilities.Description: NewNTUnicodeString does not check for string length overflow. When provided with a string that overflows the maximum size of a NTUnicodeString (a 16-bit number of bytes), it returns a truncated string rather than an error.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/tls: crypto/tls: Incorrect certificate validation during TLS session resumption
Vulnerabilities.Description: During session resumption in crypto/tls, if the underlying Config has its ClientCAs or RootCAs fields mutated between the initial handshake and the resumed handshake, the resumed handshake may succeed when it should have failed. This may happen when a user calls Config.Clone and mutates the returned Config, or uses Config.GetConfigForClient. This can cause a client to resume a session with a server that it would not have resumed with during the initial handshake, or cause a server to resume a session with a client that it would not have resumed with during the initial handshake.

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang: net/url: Memory exhaustion in query parameter parsing in net/url
Vulnerabilities.Description: The net/url package does not set a limit on the number of query parameters in a query. While the maximum size of query parameters in URLs is generally limited by the maximum request header size, the net/http.Request.ParseForm method can parse large URL-encoded forms. Parsing a large form containing many unique query parameters can cause excessive memory consumption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/x509: golang: Denial of Service due to excessive resource consumption via crafted certificate
Vulnerabilities.Description: Within HostnameError.Error(), when constructing an error string, there is no limit to the number of hosts that will be printed out. Furthermore, the error string is constructed by repeated string concatenation, leading to quadratic runtime. Therefore, a certificate provided by a malicious actor can result in excessive resource consumption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
Vulnerabilities.Description: On most platforms, Go uses the given system root certificates. However, in some narrower cases, the system trust stores may not be updated without further action. To defend against the narrower set of cases that may remain affected, a denylist was added in crypto/x509 to return an error when calling Verify with any of the known intermediate certificates that are no longer considered to be trustworthy.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/url: Incorrect parsing of IPv6 host literals in net/url
Vulnerabilities.Description: url.Parse insufficiently validated the host/authority component and accepted some invalid URLs.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
Vulnerabilities.Description: (*x509.Certificate).VerifyHostname previously called matchHostnames in a loop over all DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. This caused strings.Split(host, ".") to execute repeatedly on the same input hostname. With a large DNS SAN list, verification costs scaled quadratically based on the number of SAN entries multiplied by the hostname's label count. Because x509.Verify validates hostnames before building the certificate chain, this overhead occurred even for untrusted certificates.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/x509: crypto/tls: golang: Go: Denial of Service vulnerability in certificate chain building
Vulnerabilities.Description: During chain building, the amount of work that is done is not correctly limited when a large number of intermediate certificates are passed in VerifyOptions.Intermediates, which can lead to a denial of service. This affects both direct users of crypto/x509 and users of crypto/tls.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/x509: golang: Go crypto/x509: Denial of Service via inefficient certificate chain validation
Vulnerabilities.Description: Validating certificate chains which use policies is unexpectedly inefficient when certificates in the chain contain a very large number of policy mappings, possibly causing denial of service. This only affects validation of otherwise trusted certificate chains, issued by a root CA in the VerifyOptions.Roots CertPool, or in the system certificate pool.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/tls: golang: Go crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple TLS 1.3 key update messages
Vulnerabilities.Description: If one side of the TLS connection sends multiple key update messages post-handshake in a single record, the connection can deadlock, causing uncontrolled consumption of resources. This can lead to a denial of service. This only affects TLS 1.3.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net: golang: Go net package: Denial of Service via long CNAME response in LookupCNAME
Vulnerabilities.Description: When using LookupCNAME with the cgo DNS resolver, a very long CNAME response can trigger a double-free of C memory and a crash.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http/internal/http2: golang: golang.org/x/net: Go HTTP/2: Denial of Service via malformed SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE frame
Vulnerabilities.Description: When processing HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames, transport will enter an infinite loop of writing CONTINUATION frames if it receives a SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
Vulnerabilities.Description: Enforce a recursion limit in Unmarshal to prevent stack exhaustion when parsing deeply-nested, recursive structures.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/mail: golang: Go net/mail: Denial of Service via crafted email inputs
Vulnerabilities.Description: Well-crafted inputs reaching ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate were able to trigger excessive CPU exhaustion and memory allocations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang.org/x/net/idna: golang: net/http: golang.org/x/net/idna: Privilege escalation via incorrect Punycode label processing
Vulnerabilities.Description: The ToASCII and ToUnicode functions incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only label. For example, ToUnicode("xn--example-.com") incorrectly returns the name "example.com" rather than an error. This behavior can lead to privilege escalation in programs using the idna package. For example, a program which performs privilege checks on the ASCII hostname may reject "example.com" but permit "xn--example-.com". If that program subsequently converts the ASCII hostname to Unicode, it will inadvertently permits access to the Unicode name "example.com".

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang: Go os.Root: Symlink following vulnerability allows directory traversal
Vulnerabilities.Description: On Unix systems, opening a file in an os.Root improperly follows symlinks to locations outside of the Root when the final path component of the a path is a symbolic link and the path ends in /. For example, 'root.Open("symlink/")' will open "symlink" even when "symlink" is a symbolic link pointing outside of the root.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net: golang: Go net package: Denial of Service via NUL byte in Dial and LookupPort on Windows
Vulnerabilities.Description: The Dial and LookupPort functions panic on Windows when provided with an input containing a NUL (0).

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/mail: golang: net/mail: Denial of Service via pathological email address parsing
Vulnerabilities.Description: Pathological inputs could cause DoS through consumePhrase when parsing an email address according to RFC 5322.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mime: golang: Golang MIME: Denial of Service via maliciously-crafted MIME header
Vulnerabilities.Description: Decoding a maliciously-crafted MIME header containing many invalid encoded-words can consume excessive CPU.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
Vulnerabilities.Description: When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads a few bytes from each new connection to see if they contain the HTTP/2 client preface. ReadHeaderTimeout is unexpectedly not being applied when doing this.

Vulnerabilities.Title: html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input
Vulnerabilities.Description: Previously, pathological inputs could close an unescaped '/' early, allowing for attack-controlled data to inject arbitrary content, potentially leading to XSS.

Vulnerabilities.Title: encoding/xml: golang: Go: Denial of Service via XML decoding recursion depth issue
Vulnerabilities.Description: Previously, DecodeElement would reset the depth counter causing it to never fire; this could lead to stack exhaustion.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution
Vulnerabilities.Description: Previously, resolving relative paths containing parent directory ('..') segments performed string conversions and buffer rewrites on each step, resulting in quadratic time complexity and high memory allocation overhead. Now, path resolution operates on a byte buffer using index-based backtracking for '..' segments, eliminating the quadratic time complexity and significantly reducing memory allocations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
Vulnerabilities.Description: Handshake messages, such as KeyUpdate, are always considered as state-advancing, regardless of whether a handshake has been completed or not. As a result, a malicious client can keep sending KeyUpdate messages to force the server to keep performing key derivation operations indefinitely.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
Vulnerabilities.Description: When parsing a Range header containing a large number of small ranges, FileServer(FS), ServeContent, and ServeFile(FS) can consume an excessive amount of CPU.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
Vulnerabilities.Description: A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption in the client or server by opening a large number of streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple ECH outer extension references
Vulnerabilities.Description: Multiple ECH outer extension references are not permitted under RFC 9849; previously, a client could send a well-crafted packet that could trigger memory exhaustion in the server process by specifying multiple references. We now reject these as malformed and curb the memory amplification vector as a result.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/url: Insufficient validation of bracketed IPv6 hostnames in net/url
Vulnerabilities.Description: The Parse function permits values other than IPv6 addresses to be included in square brackets within the host component of a URL. RFC 3986 permits IPv6 addresses to be included within the host component, enclosed within square brackets. For example: "http://[::1]/". IPv4 addresses and hostnames must not appear within square brackets. Parse did not enforce this requirement.

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang: archive/tar: Unbounded allocation when parsing GNU sparse map
Vulnerabilities.Description: tar.Reader does not set a maximum size on the number of sparse region data blocks in GNU tar pax 1.0 sparse files. A maliciously-crafted archive containing a large number of sparse regions can cause a Reader to read an unbounded amount of data from the archive into memory. When reading from a compressed source, a small compressed input can result in large allocations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: encoding/asn1: Parsing DER payload can cause memory exhaustion in encoding/asn1
Vulnerabilities.Description: Parsing a maliciously crafted DER payload could allocate large amounts of memory, causing memory exhaustion.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/x509: Quadratic complexity when checking name constraints in crypto/x509
Vulnerabilities.Description: Due to the design of the name constraint checking algorithm, the processing time of some inputs scale non-linearly with respect to the size of the certificate. This affects programs which validate arbitrary certificate chains.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/x509: golang: Panic when validating certificates with DSA public keys in crypto/x509
Vulnerabilities.Description: Validating certificate chains which contain DSA public keys can cause programs to panic, due to a interface cast that assumes they implement the Equal method. This affects programs which validate arbitrary certificate chains.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/tls: go crypto/tls ALPN negotiation error contains attacker controlled information
Vulnerabilities.Description: When Conn.Handshake fails during ALPN negotiation the error contains attacker controlled information (the ALPN protocols sent by the client) which is not escaped.

Vulnerabilities.Title: encoding/pem: Quadratic complexity when parsing some invalid inputs in encoding/pem
Vulnerabilities.Description: The processing time for parsing some invalid inputs scales non-linearly with respect to the size of the input. This affects programs which parse untrusted PEM inputs.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/textproto: Excessive CPU consumption in Reader.ReadResponse in net/textproto
Vulnerabilities.Description: The Reader.ReadResponse function constructs a response string through repeated string concatenation of lines. When the number of lines in a response is large, this can cause excessive CPU consumption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/mail: Excessive CPU consumption in ParseAddress in net/mail
Vulnerabilities.Description: The ParseAddress function constructs domain-literal address components through repeated string concatenation. When parsing large domain-literal components, this can cause excessive CPU consumption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang: crypto/x509: excluded subdomain constraint does not restrict wildcard SANs
Vulnerabilities.Description: An excluded subdomain constraint in a certificate chain does not restrict the usage of wildcard SANs in the leaf certificate. For example a constraint that excludes the subdomain test.example.com does not prevent a leaf certificate from claiming the SAN *.example.com.

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang: archive/zip: Excessive CPU consumption when building archive index in archive/zip
Vulnerabilities.Description: archive/zip uses a super-linear file name indexing algorithm that is invoked the first time a file in an archive is opened. This can lead to a denial of service when consuming a maliciously constructed ZIP archive.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/tls: Handshake messages may be processed at the incorrect encryption level in crypto/tls
Vulnerabilities.Description: During the TLS 1.3 handshake if multiple messages are sent in records that span encryption level boundaries (for instance the Client Hello and Encrypted Extensions messages), the subsequent messages may be processed before the encryption level changes. This can cause some minor information disclosure if a network-local attacker can inject messages during the handshake.

Vulnerabilities.Title: html/template: URLs in meta content attribute actions are not escaped in html/template
Vulnerabilities.Description: Actions which insert URLs into the content attribute of HTML meta tags are not escaped. This can allow XSS if the meta tag also has an http-equiv attribute with the value "refresh". A new GODEBUG setting has been added, htmlmetacontenturlescape, which can be used to disable escaping URLs in actions in the meta content attribute which follow "url=" by setting htmlmetacontenturlescape=0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang: internal/syscall/unix: Root.Chmod can follow symlinks out of the root
Vulnerabilities.Description: On Linux, if the target of Root.Chmod is replaced with a symlink while the chmod operation is in progress, Chmod can operate on the target of the symlink, even when the target lies outside the root. The Linux fchmodat syscall silently ignores the AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW flag, which Root.Chmod uses to avoid symlink traversal. Root.Chmod checks its target before acting and returns an error if the target is a symlink lying outside the root, so the impact is limited to cases where the target is replaced with a symlink between the check and operation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: archive/tar: golang: Go's archive/tar package: Denial of Service via maliciously-crafted archive
Vulnerabilities.Description: tar.Reader can allocate an unbounded amount of memory when reading a maliciously-crafted archive containing a large number of sparse regions encoded in the "old GNU sparse map" format.

Vulnerabilities.Title: html/template: golang: html/template: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via improper context and brace depth tracking in JS template literals
Vulnerabilities.Description: Context was not properly tracked across template branches for JS template literals, leading to possibly incorrect escaping of content when branches were used. Additionally template actions within JS template literals did not properly track the brace depth, leading to incorrect escaping being applied. These issues could cause actions within JS template literals to be incorrectly or improperly escaped, leading to XSS vulnerabilities.

Vulnerabilities.Title: html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via improper URL escaping in meta tag content
Vulnerabilities.Description: CVE-2026-27142 fixed a vulnerability in which URLs were not correctly escaped inside of a <meta> tag's <content> attribute. If the URL content were to insert ASCII whitespaces around the '=' rune inside of the <content> attribute, the escaper would fail to similarly escape it, leading to XSS.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http/httputil: golang: net/http/httputil: ReverseProxy forwards hidden query parameters, potentially bypassing security controls
Vulnerabilities.Description: ReverseProxy can forward queries containing parameters not visible to Rewrite functions. When used with a Rewrite function, or a Director function which parses query parameters, ReverseProxy sanitizes the forwarded request to remove query parameters which are not parsed by url.ParseQuery. ReverseProxy does not take ParseQuery's limit on the total number of query parameters (controlled by GODEBUG=urlmaxqueryparams=N) into account. This can permit ReverseProxy to forward a request containing a query parameter that is not visible to the Rewrite function. For example, the query "a1=x&a2=x&...&a10000=x&hidden=y" can forward the parameter "hidden=y" while hiding it from the proxy's Rewrite function.

Vulnerabilities.Title: html/template: golang: html/template: Cross-site scripting due to incorrect script tag escaping
Vulnerabilities.Description: If a trusted template author were to write a <script> tag containing an empty 'type' attribute or a 'type' attribute with an ASCII whitespace, the execution of the template would incorrectly escape any data passed into the <script> block.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/tls: golang: Go crypto/tls: Information disclosure in Encrypted Client Hello
Vulnerabilities.Description: Handshakes which used Encrypted Client Hello could be de-anonymized by a passive network observer due to a disclosure of pre-shared key identities in the unencrypted client hello.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/textproto: golang: Golang net/textproto: Misleading error messages via input injection
Vulnerabilities.Description: When returning errors, functions in the net/textproto package would include its input as part of the error. This might allow an attacker to inject misleading content to errors that are printed or logged.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: golang: golang: Cross-user response poisoning via desynchronized HTTP CONNECT connections
Vulnerabilities.Description: When http.Transport sends an HTTP/1 CONNECT request with a non-empty Request.Body, it writes the body directly to the connection without framing after the request headers. If the server rejects the CONNECT request with a non-2xx keep-alive response, Transport returns the connection to the idle pool. Because CONNECT requests do not have a request body, the server may interpret the trailing body bytes as a subsequent pipelined HTTP/1.1 request on the connection, leaving the pooled connection desynchronized and causing the next caller that reuses it to read the response to the injected request. In reverse proxies (including httputil.ReverseProxy) that forward CONNECT requests through a shared Transport, this can lead to cross-user response poisoning.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: net/http: Denial of Service via HTTP/2 trailer header memory exhaustion
Vulnerabilities.Description: When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP server internally uses the header values to populate the Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers, which do not support multiplexing a large number of requests over one TCP connection, and whose Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: golang: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: HTTP response smuggling via malformed HTTP/2 framing headers
Vulnerabilities.Description: Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does not behave strictly enough, this can result in response smuggling.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang: golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass via double refund in HTTP/2 server
Vulnerabilities.Description: The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the stream), and again when a request handler reads the buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is still limited by the concurrent stream limit and stream-level flow control.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: golang: net/http: HTTP request smuggling via improper handling of HTTP/1 CONNECT responses
Vulnerabilities.Description: When an HTTP server handler sends a 2xx response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT request and returns without hijacking the connection, the server improperly continues to read and serve requests from the connection. Since a 2xx response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT converts the connection into a tunnel, the server should not treat the connection as continuing to contain HTTP. The impact of this misbehavior is mostly limited to potential request smuggling, where an intermediate proxy considers the data on the connection to be tunneled and the server considers it to be HTTP.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/textproto: mime/multipart: golang: golang: Denial of Service via memory limit bypass in multipart form parsing
Vulnerabilities.Description: Parsing a multipart form can bypass memory limits and read an arbitrarily long line into memory when the remaining limit at the start of a part is less than 400 bytes.

Vulnerabilities.Title: html/template: golang: golang: cross-site scripting via consecutive expressions in JavaScript template literals
Vulnerabilities.Description: When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive expressions, the context tracking state was not properly reset upon entering a new expression. We now ensure that template-literal expression entries correctly reset context variables so all subsequent regular expression literals are accurately recognized and escaped.

Vulnerabilities.Title: html/template: golang: html/template: Cross-site scripting via improper escaping of yield keyword
Vulnerabilities.Description: A trusted template author may have previously written a valid template wherein the use of the 'yield' keyword would not be correctly escaped. We now ensure that valid keyword uses are escaped and non-keyword uses are not escaped.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via concurrent HPACK encoder modification
Vulnerabilities.Description: HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when handling a SETTINGS frame containing SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious client can repeatedly send a request while changing the header table size to crash the server.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: golang: net/http: Denial of Service via race condition when handling oversized HTTP/1 requests
Vulnerabilities.Description: For HTTP/1 servers, when MaxBytesReader's limit is exceeded, "Connection: close" header is automatically set without synchronization, which might race with another header being set explicitly in the server handler. As a result, an HTTP/1 server that utilizes MaxBytesReader or MaxBytesHandler can crash due to runtime panic if its handler reads the request body concurrently with writing the response header.

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang.org/net/http: Lack of limit when parsing cookies can cause memory exhaustion in net/http
Vulnerabilities.Description: Despite HTTP headers having a default limit of 1MB, the number of cookies that can be parsed does not have a limit. By sending a lot of very small cookies such as "a=;", an attacker can make an HTTP server allocate a large amount of structs, causing large memory consumption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: os: FileInfo can escape from a Root in golang os module
Vulnerabilities.Description: On Unix platforms, when listing the contents of a directory using File.ReadDir or File.Readdir the returned FileInfo could reference a file outside of the Root in which the File was opened. The impact of this escape is limited to reading metadata provided by lstat from arbitrary locations on the filesystem without permitting reading or writing files outside the root.

Vulnerabilities.Title: os: golang: golang: Directory traversal via Windows junction handling
Vulnerabilities.Description: On Windows, when the target of Root.Mkdir or Root.MkdirAll is a junction pointing to an empty location, the operation can create a directory at the junction target even when that target is located outside the root. This only applies to operations where the last path component is a junction (path/to/junction, but not path/junction/target).
